universe.membership_rule: inner join to momentum_events_canonical WHERE in_scope = TRUE
universe.materialization_note: Reused verbatim from config/fundamentals_f1.json -- a live SELECT against momentum_events_canonical is pathologically slow regardless of projected columns (the view's staged construction joins filtered_trades/filtered_quotes for coverage flags unconditionally). E1-T0 checks set equality against this materialization, not a live view scan, exactly as research/fundamentals_f1/verify_event_fundamentals.py already does.

tape_side.detection_price_source_note: Reused, not re-derived (reuse-before-build/D30) -- F1-T6 already built a D4-compliant, tick-derived detection_price and detection_price_decile for all 20,951 events. E1 does not re-read v2_r13_detection/a102_detection_anchors/first-trade fallback itself.
tape_side.event_volume_and_prints_source: computed fresh in E1-T0/T4 directly from filtered_trades via DuckDB SQL, joined through momentum_events_canonical WHERE in_scope, grouped per event -- never materialized to a dataframe (CLAUDE.md: DuckDB SQL over pandas)
tape_side.event_volume_window: full event_date_canonical regular session (09:30-16:00 America/New_York, XNYS calendar) -- a single declared window, not a horizon grid. No sub-session-boundary arithmetic of the kind that produced phase/13's HARD STOP.
tape_side.session_bucketing: each print classified pre-market (<09:30) / regular (09:30-16:00) / after-hours (>16:00) America/New_York, XNYS session calendar, same pinned convention as CLAUDE.md's Session calendar rule

deciles.labels: 0=lowest, 9=highest (or fewer bins if qcut drops duplicate edges -- reported, not hidden)

min_cell_n_display_floor_note: Below this, a table/heatmap cell is shown as 'n<20' rather than a computed statistic -- display-floor only, never a population filter (brief SS4: 'does not filter the population on coverage').

subsampling.note: Disclosed in-caption per any chart whose raw overlay is sub-sampled, per research-charts skill SS2.

chart_theme.source: copied by value from research/phase_13/chart_common.py (most recent), matching phase_6/8/9/11 and fundamentals_f1's inline usage
chart_theme.deviation_from_brief: brief SS3 said 'dark theme' -- no dark-theme chart exists anywhere in this repo's history, treated as a drafting slip. See prompts/fundamental_exploration_e1.md SS7.
